Problem stem: A thermostat is modeled by $T(t) = \begin{cases} 68 + 2t & t < 5 \\ 80 - t & t \geq 5 \end{cases}$. Find $\lim_{t \to 5^-} T(t)$ and $\lim_{t \to 5^+} T(t)$. Does $\lim_{t \to 5} T(t)$ exist?
Available first step: Identify which piece of the function applies when t is slightly less than 5.
Keep the response at or below 150 words.
When we write $\lim_{t \to 5^-}$, we're looking at values of $t$ that are just barely less than $5$. Which formula in the piecewise definition applies when $t < 5$?

Problem stem: Prove that if $\lim_{x \to c} f(x) = L$, then both $\lim_{x \to c^-} f(x) = L$ and $\lim_{x \to c^+} f(x) = L$.
Available first step: Start from the epsilon-delta definition of the two-sided limit and show it implies the one-sided definitions.
Keep the response at or below 150 words.

Write out the $\epsilon$-$\delta$ definition: for every $\epsilon > 0$ there exists $\delta > 0$ such that $0 < |x - c| < \delta \Rightarrow |f(x) - L| < \epsilon$. Now, the left-hand limit restricts attention to $x$ satisfying $c - \delta < x < c$. Does every such $x$ also satisfy $0 < |x - c| < \delta$? What does that tell you?
